en.headline: Garden Company apologises after crowd chaos at student sandwich event
en.dek: The bakery said no one was injured when parents pushing to collect children broke a door handle at the Wan Chai school hall.
body: The Garden Company has apologised and promised to review crowd-management arrangements after an event involving more than 700 primary pupils descended into confusion at the end.

The company held a world-record attempt for the largest sandwich-making lesson on Sunday at SKH Tang Shiu Kin Secondary School in Wan Chai to mark its approaching 100th anniversary. Pupils from about 100 schools had 30 minutes to make sandwiches. Attendees later posted online that the session overran by nearly an hour and that entrance and exit were not separated.

Garden confirmed that at the close of the event a large number of people were waiting and some parents pushed forward, causing a door handle to come off. The company said staff controlled the situation, no one was injured, and there was no fighting. It said it would examine admission and crowd-control procedures for future large events.
Parents who spoke to media described long waits, unclear instructions and overcrowding, though the company maintained that all students left safely with their families.

zh.headline: 嘉頓就學生三文治活動散場混亂致歉 承諾檢討人流安排
zh.dek: 公司指無人受傷，部分家長推撞令禮堂大門門柄脫落，將審視日後大型活動入場及人流管制。
body: 本地麵包品牌嘉頓就周日在灣仔一所中學舉行的大型活動結束時出現混亂，公開道歉並承諾檢討。
嘉頓為慶祝即將迎來100周年，於聖公會鄧肇堅中學禮堂舉辦「最大規模的三文治製作課程」世界紀錄挑戰，逾700名來自約100間小學的學生參與，需在30分鐘內親手製作三文治。事後有家長在網上反映活動超時近一小時，出入口未有分流，散場時情況混亂。
嘉頓確認活動結束時現場人數眾多、等候時間較長，部分家長急於會合而出現推撞，導致大門門柄脫落。公司指工作人員已即時控制場面，無人受傷，亦無發生網上傳聞的打架事件，並會全面審視日後大型活動的入場機制及人流管制。
有家長向傳媒表示等候時間長、指示不清及場地擁擠，但公司強調所有學生均安全回到家長身邊。
